nodes.label: Recovery of Fully Supervised Performance with 19 Percent Labels
nodes.rationale: The plan evaluates how much of the Part A DeepLabV3 result each SSL method recovers when fine-tuned on only 2,553 labelled slices, about 19 percent of the Part A training labels.

nodes.label: LiTS 256x256 Liver and Tumor CT Dataset
Part A Split to Part B Role Remapping
nodes.rationale: The saved Part A split is reused without rebuilding so Part A and Part B remain leakage-safe and directly comparable: train becomes unlabelled pretraining, validation becomes labelled fine-tuning, and test becomes monitoring plus final evaluation.

nodes.label: Test Split Double Role Disclosure
nodes.rationale: Checkpoint selection touches the test split, making reported metrics mildly optimistic; a fourth truly held-out split is described as infeasible because the labelled set is small, so the limitation must be disclosed.

nodes.label: Course Lab Notebook Backbone Convention
nodes.rationale: The plan follows the course labs, which use ResNet-50 for SimCLR, BYOL, and CNN-MAE so their encoders transfer directly into the Part A DeepLabV3 backbone; only DINOv2 uses a ViT adapter.

nodes.label: ResNet-50 CNN-MAE
nodes.rationale: Although the assignment lists a ViT as the typical MAE backbone, the plan deliberately adopts the course lab's ResNet-50 CNN-MAE because it transfers directly and methodologically cleanly into the reused DeepLabV3 backbone.

nodes.label: DINOv2 Token-to-Grid ASPP Adapter
nodes.rationale: The adapter drops the CLS token, reshapes patch tokens into a 16 by 16 spatial grid, and uses smaller ASPP dilation rates because the ViT feature grid is only 16 by 16.

nodes.label: DINOv2 Frozen Warm-up then Fine-tuning
nodes.rationale: DINOv2 is selected for the required frozen-versus-fine-tuned experiment: the ASPP head is warmed up for two epochs with the encoder frozen, then the encoder is unfrozen with separate learning rates.

nodes.label: Float32 SSL Loss under AMP
nodes.rationale: Contrastive, regression, and reconstruction losses are evaluated in float32 even when AMP is enabled to avoid half-precision overflow and numerical instability.

nodes.label: Ten-Minute Notebook Split Threshold
nodes.rationale: A method is split into pretraining and downstream notebooks when measured per-epoch time exceeds ten minutes, preventing fifty epochs from overrunning the Kaggle session limit.

nodes.label: Data Prep to SimCLR to BYOL to MAE to DINOv2 Build Order
nodes.rationale: SimCLR follows data preparation because it is the cheapest end-to-end method for validating encoder, ASPP, fine-tuning, and metric plumbing before scaling to more expensive methods.

nodes.label: Part B AI Usage Compliance
nodes.rationale: AI may scaffold boilerplate, debugging, and API use, but the group must write Insights, error-analysis reasoning, and viva answers; non-trivial AI-assisted code requires a disclosure comment.

nodes.label: Question-to-Notebook-Cell Pointer Checklist
nodes.rationale: The policy-safe viva artifact maps expected questions to the exact notebook cells that contain evidence, while leaving the answers for group members to formulate themselves.

nodes.label: Fixed Part A Baseline
nodes.rationale: The Part A tumor score is not improved during Part B so the fully supervised baseline remains a fixed comparison target.

nodes.label: SSL-for-Segmentation Five-Stage Pipeline
nodes.rationale: An image passes through a pretrained SSL encoder to dense patch features, then the reused Part A decoder upsamples those features to a class label per pixel; the encoder can be frozen or fine-tuned.
nodes.author: Dr. Md Rifat Ahmmad Rashid

nodes.label: Label-Efficiency Comparison
nodes.rationale: The assignment's central comparison asks how closely SSL-pretrained models approach the Part A fully supervised baseline when fine-tuned with far fewer labelled images.
nodes.author: Dr. Md Rifat Ahmmad Rashid

nodes.label: Leakage-Safe Split Role Mapping
nodes.rationale: The Part A split must be reused without re-splitting or reshuffling so the Part A versus Part B comparison stays fair and images do not leak across roles.
nodes.author: Dr. Md Rifat Ahmmad Rashid

nodes.author: Dr. Md Rifat Ahmmad Rashid

nodes.label: Test Split Double Role Caveat
nodes.rationale: The test split deliberately serves both checkpoint selection and final evaluation because holding out a fourth split would leave too little labelled fine-tuning data; this departs from strict practice and can inflate metrics.
nodes.author: Dr. Md Rifat Ahmmad Rashid

nodes.label: BYOL Online Network and EMA Target
nodes.rationale: BYOL avoids negative pairs by training an online network to predict the representation of a differently augmented view produced by a stop-gradient target network updated as an exponential moving average.
nodes.author: Dr. Md Rifat Ahmmad Rashid

nodes.label: Official Checkpoint Continuation
nodes.rationale: Continuing self-supervised training from an official ImageNet-pretrained checkpoint for fifty epochs is the recommended default because full random-initialization SSL pretraining can take days on free Kaggle GPUs.
nodes.author: Dr. Md Rifat Ahmmad Rashid

nodes.label: Pretrain and Downstream Notebook Stage Split
nodes.rationale: When either stage exceeds ten minutes per epoch, it may be split into a pretraining notebook that saves an encoder checkpoint and a downstream notebook that reloads it, avoiding an eight-to-nine-hour session overrun.
nodes.author: Dr. Md Rifat Ahmmad Rashid

nodes.label: Reuse of the Best Part A Decoder Head
nodes.rationale: Each SSL encoder must use the same decoder design that performed best in Part A so the experiment changes representation learning while preserving the downstream head.
nodes.author: Dr. Md Rifat Ahmmad Rashid

nodes.label: ViT Patch-Token to Spatial-Grid Adapter
nodes.rationale: ViT token sequences must be reshaped into a two-dimensional feature map before the Part A decoder can perform spatial upsampling and per-pixel classification.
nodes.author: Dr. Md Rifat Ahmmad Rashid

nodes.label: Two-Column LaTeX Report
nodes.rationale: The final report must use a standard two-column conference-style LaTeX layout, span approximately four to six pages, and omit a literature review section.
nodes.author: Dr. Md Rifat Ahmmad Rashid

nodes.label: AI Usage Policy
nodes.rationale: AI assistants are permitted for boilerplate code, debugging, and library API understanding but may not generate the Insights section, error-analysis reasoning, or viva answers.
